newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SAPEC AIMS TO CONTROL QUIMIGAL'S FERTILISER ARM.
newsitem.headline: SAPEC AIMS TO CONTROL QUIMIGAL'S FERTILISER ARM.

text.p: Belgian holding company Sapec SA said on Monday it had taken part in the privatisation of Portugese chemicals company Quimigal with a view to gaining control over Quimigal's fertiliser arm.

Portuguese firm Quimigest, in which Sapec is a partner, won the bidding for a 90 percent stake in Quimigal-Quimica de Portugal SA with a 8.14 billion escudo offer on Thursday. The deal will give Sapec 25 percent in Quimigal in a first phase.

Before the end of the year Sapec would sell that stake back to the Mello group, which owned 75 percent of Quimigest- Sociedade Quimica de Prestacao de Servicos, in return for 49 percent in Quimigal Adubos, Quimigal's fertiliser arm.
The transaction would raise Sapec's investment to 2.47 billion escudo (510 million francs) from some two billion escudo for the initial 25 percent stake.
Once legal constraints were lifted Sapec would raise its stake in Quimigal Adubos to 50 percent. Sapec and Mello would jointly manage the unit.

Finally, Quimigal Adubos would buy Sapec's fertiliser unit. The two would be merged to achieve industrial and logistical synergies. Terms of this deal were still being negotiated. "Overall the total of the operations would not bring a notable increase in debt with it," Sapec said in its statement.
The joint unit would have production capacity in excess of one million tonnes, have 17 percent of the Iberian market and be one of the top five producers in Europe.
Quimigal Adubos had 1996 turnover of 23 billion escudos, cashflow of 2.83 billion and net profit of 1.6 billion. Shareholders equity was 8.8 billion.
The outlook for the current year was for a slight downturn given the less favourable shape the sector was in in Europe.
Trade in shares in Sapec on Brussels' double-fixing cash market was halted for the day. Sapec closed at 1,510 francs on Thursday. Friday was a one-day market holiday in Belgium.
Belgian Cobepa holds 12.43 percent of Sapec. Group Financiere Frederic Jacobs and group Espirito Santo have 62.64 percent.
